title: Reserved Capacity and Savings Plan Utilization (Multi-Cloud)

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:billing` events with `lineItem_LineItemType=*Reserved* OR lineItem_LineItemType=*Savings*` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.9 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:billing` traffic without `lineItem_LineItemType=*Reserved* OR lineItem_LineItemType=*Savings*`. Confirm UC-4.4.9 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via Combined cloud TAs, billing and usage exports; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Combined cloud TAs, billing and usage exports
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" lineItem_LineItemType=*Reserved* OR lineItem_LineItemType=*Savings*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress

description: UC-4.4.9 — Reserved Capacity and Savings Plan Utilization (Multi-Cloud): queries Microsoft Azure `aws:billing` for search criteria `lineItem_LineItemType=*Reserved* OR lineItem_LineItemType=*Savings*` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Reserved Capacity and Savings Plan Utilization (Multi-Cloud)' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.9 drives low-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest reservation and usage data from each provider. Calculate utilization (used vs. committed). Dashboard utilization by type and account/project. Alert when utilization < 70% to trigger right-sizing or exchange.
visualization: Table (reservation, type, utilization %), Gauge (overall utilization), Bar chart (waste by type).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Combined cloud TAs, billing and usage exports with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest reservation and usage data from each provider. Calculate utilization (used vs. committed). Dashboard utilization by type and account/project. Alert when utilization < 70% to trigger right-sizing or exchange.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" lineItem_LineItemType=*Reserved* OR lineItem_LineItemType=*Savings*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.9_reserved_capacity_and_sa_9"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=aws` to detect reserved capacity and savings plan utilization (multi-cloud). Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_9_alert` with severity aligned to `low` criticality. Dashboard: Table (reservation, type, utilization %), Gauge (overall utilization), Bar chart (waste by type)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Combined cloud TAs, billing and usage exports and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of reserved capacity and savings plan utilization (multi-cloud) so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
